newsitem.title: UK: Lufthansa Cargo starts UK cost-cutting.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo starts UK cost-cutting.

text.p: The UK division of Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCAG) has embarked on a three-pronged attack on cost-cutting to help its parent company, a unit of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, return to profitability, UK and Ireland marketing manager Ruediger Helm said.

"We aim to do this by raising our prices, by reducing the number of overtime hours worked by staff and by making equipment cost savings. But we do not plan any cut in the number of employees, which currently total about 230 in the UK," he told Reuters in an interview.

On February 24, Lufthansa Cargo senior vice-president Europe and Africa Joachim Haas said that unless LCAG, which made a yet-to-be-disclosed loss for 1996, did achieve profitability by 1998, it would be re-integrated as part of the airline's passenger division.

Helm said that LCAG UK contributed between five and 10 percent of Lufthansa Cargo's overall revenues. In 1996, he added, the UK unit increased its revenues by nearly 12 percent and made a small profit, but he declined to give details.

"For 1997, we have been given a target by head office of achieving another 12 to 13 percent revenue rise. We are helped here by the strength of sterling against the mark and taking this, and our cost-cutting measures into consideration, I am sure we will reach this target and also make another small, but improved profit," he said.
Helm said that the highest ex-UK rate increases, all of which come into effect on April 1, would relate to LCAG's "Flash" express product.

"Flash' was launched in September 1993, and represents 30 percent of our business in the UK, with general cargo accounting for 60 percent and special products -- such as the transportation of animals, dangerous goods, Formula One cars and so on -- 10 percent," he added.
"We see the ratio of our Flash' business increasing to 40 percent of the total in the UK in the next two to three years and eventually to 50 percent," he said.
Helm added that ex-UK "Flash" rates would go up by 10 percent to Germany and central Europe and by 15 percent to eastern Europe and to some areas in the Far East.

General cargo rates from the UK would go up by 20 percent to eastern Europe, five percent to Japan and Korea, five percent to the Middle East, five percent to Africa and from seven to eight percent to Latin America. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
